## Body

# #337 (F281) review at 4fd7426: pass-with-notes

No blocker. Limits, filter detection, kill scope, quoting and ledger are right. Six notes for the author, none of them a normal-use bug.

## Checked and holding
- Kill scope (rule 6): only `-$child` (cargo's group), the monitor's group and the relay pids. No kill by pattern. INT, TERM and HUP mid-run: rc 130/143/129; monitor, relays, cargo group and lock all gone (probed).
- cargo's status survives the relay: a fake `cargo test` exiting 101 makes the script exit 101 (probed).
- FIFOs sit inside the lock dir, which `mkdir -m 0700` creates atomically. No predictable-name race, and `rm -rf` of the lock removes them.
- Stop message: `printf %s` of the last test line and the args. No eval, no injection.
- No polling: the monitor blocks in `read -t` up to the nearest deadline.
- has_filter: probed `-v`, `--no-fail-fast`, `--exact`, `--ignored`, `--skip=a`, `--message-format json`, `-Zunstable-options --format json` (none filter) and `--include-ignored foo` (filters). All correct.
- Privacy: no paths, accounts or emails in the added lines.
- Ledger: diff against current origin/main `docs/difficulties.md` is exactly the D-F281-1 row. Clean resolution.
- Mutants (mine): M1, idle clock armed from the start instead of the first `Running` line: KILLED. M2, `--skip` dropped from the value list: KILLED. M3: see N6.

## Notes (author fixes; prime checks)
- N1, exit paths: `on_signal` and `on_exit` never stop the relays. A signal that lands after the relays fork but before cargo opens the FIFOs leaves both relays blocked forever in `open()` on FIFOs that `rm -rf` has already unlinked: two leaked bash processes, no CPU. Adjacent case observed: an INT about 40 ms in left the fake cargo and both relays running after the lock was released. The cargo half of that window predates this PR (main has `cargo &` then `child=$!`); leaking the relays is new. Fix: after drain, `kill -TERM -- -$pid` for each relay group in both traps.
- N2, cost, rule 5 letter: the relays and the monitor run at the caller's niceness. ps showed them at `S` next to cargo at `SN`. Relay CPU is about 4 s per MB: 40k lines (2.3 MB) took 19.9 s wall and 9.4 s CPU from a nice-19 caller. A real workspace run is about 3k lines, so under 1 s. Fix: renice the relays and the monitor to 19 (once per run), or state the exception in AGENTS.md.
- N3, wrong attribution: serial libtest (`--test-threads=1`) prints `test b ... ` with no newline until b ends, and prints no 60 s warning. The relay holds that partial line, so the idle stop message names the PREVIOUS test (`last test line: test a ... ok`) while b is the one hung. Observed. Fix: call it the last completed test line, or have the monitor track a partial `test ` prefix.
- N4, cosmetic: once the monitor exits (a limit fell), the relay's `printf >&7` fails, and bash 3.2 later flushes that line's stdio buffer to the relay's own fd. The result is duplicate lines (`test b_hangs ... ` twice) and stray blank lines after a stop. Observed. Fix: on the first failed write, close fd 7 and stop forwarding.
- N5, arming (reasoned): `*"Running "*` also matches the compile lines `cargo test -v` prints (`Running \`rustc ...\``). A verbose run therefore arms the idle and filtered clocks while still compiling, and a rustc silent for over 2 min under load gets stopped. Fix: match only cargo's test-binary line, for example require that no backtick follows `Running `.
- N6, witness gap: M3 (`return 0` in place of `return "$status"` on the relay path) SURVIVES all 31 tests. The real code is right (101 probed), but nothing witnesses it. Add one test: a failing `cargo test` exits with cargo's status.

Policy note (not a finding): with libtest's 60 s warning, a healthy single test silent for more than about 180 s (multi-thread) or 120 s (serial) is stopped. That is Jordan's strict-on-purpose ruling, so it should be stated as such.
